headers.//: Asset URLs carry no version, so a browser holding a cached copy of one release's JavaScript can run it against the next release's HTML. That mix is worse than either version alone: it looks like data failing to arrive. GitHub Pages was handled by stamping every URL with the commit; here the answer is to revalidate, which costs one 304 and cannot go wrong.
The pages themselves, for the same reason and more so.
The site is same-origin apart from Google Fonts and the Supabase project, and it is never framed. Said in headers because a browser will enforce these and a policy document will not.
